blockingIssues.description: The auth E2E suite never polls the returned operationId/pollUrl for signup or signin, so VAL-E2E-001/002 can regress without failing the tests.
Auth refresh still does not reliably issue a new JWT because SetAccessCookie only varies second-resolution claims and the tests only assert a non-empty cookie.
GitHub OAuth start/callback handling does not generate or validate a session-bound state parameter, leaving the flow vulnerable to OAuth CSRF/account-linking attacks.
CreateProject and UpdateProject ignore database Exec errors, so operations can report success even when writes fail or duplicate-slug races occur.
RepoImport accepts any parseable URI such as ftp://bad instead of enforcing the required GitHub HTTPS repository URL contract.
The new multi-language build paths still execute host-installed toolchains instead of containerized builds, so the milestone's isolation/toolchain requirement is unmet.
Python, JS/TS, and .NET detection heuristics are too broad and can classify ordinary repos as supported instead of failing with buildStrategy "unknown".

Several component-language build commands do not match the documented toolchains, including hardcoded world names for Python/JS and a standalone componentize-dotnet path instead of the researched dotnet/MSBuild integration.
ArtifactUploadRoute still returns a synchronous 201 response instead of the required 202 async operation envelope.
Uploaded artifact builds are stored as build_strategy "uploaded_artifact" instead of the required "prebuilt_wasm" strategy.
DeleteDeployment only updates database state; the runtime abstraction has no stop/terminate path, so DELETE does not guarantee the WASM runtime is actually shut down.
The added deployment tests do not verify polling to a running deployment result with runtimeEndpoint/domainBinding, successful upload flows, runtime 2xx access, or shutdown after deletion.
The operation-envelope coverage omits POST /api/v1/uploads/source-bundles, so it does not yet verify the 202 async envelope contract across every relevant mutating endpoint.

appliedUpdates.description: Added .factory/library/e2e-pipeline.md documenting the GitHub OAuth env vars, the concrete async operation-submitting routes, the GitHub HTTPS repo-import contract, and the repo research file that defines containerized/component-language WASM build expectations.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Require transcript/handoff evidence for backend API manual verification (`curl.exe` plus `interactiveChecks`) and failing-test-first TDD before workers can claim `followedProcedure=true`, or document an explicit exception path when manual verification is impossible.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: All six e2e-pipeline feature reviews (e2e-auth-flow, e2e-github-oauth, e2e-project-repo, e2e-wasm-languages, e2e-deployment-access, e2e-operations-logs) reported the same mismatch: handoffs marked `followedProcedure=true` while transcript evidence showed no manual curl verification, no interactiveChecks, and in several cases no red-phase targeted test before implementation.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add an explicit OAuth security convention that any third-party OAuth start/callback flow must generate, persist, and validate a session-bound `state` parameter before accepting the callback.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The e2e-github-oauth review found `backend/janus-api/internal/api/handler/github_oauth.go` implemented start/callback handling without any `state` parameter, and AGENTS.md currently only provides a broad security rule rather than an OAuth-specific requirement.

rejectedObservations.observation: Repeated backend-worker procedure-enforcement observations across all six e2e-pipeline reviews.
rejectedObservations.reason: duplicate; consolidated into one backend-worker skill recommendation in suggestedGuidanceUpdates.
